channel.title: Redock
channel.description: Updates for Redock, a window manager for macOS.

item.title: Version 1.9.3
item.description:
• Redock is now signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple. It opens normally on first launch; no right-click Open step, no Privacy & Security detour.
  • The price shown inside the app now matches checkout: £19.99 once for three Macs.

item.title: Version 1.9.2
item.description:
• Purchase-success pages and licence emails can now open Redock and activate this Mac automatically through a signed, expiring link. The licence key remains available as a fallback.
  • Workspace, app-rule, drag-zone and Clipboard Pro prompts now preview the specific result you asked for and can start the 14-day trial directly.
  • Save a Workspace and Pro clipboard actions now lead to their contextual offer instead of a generic licence screen.

item.title: Version 1.9.1
item.description:
• Redock now checks for signed updates at launch when its previous check is more than a day old, and brings an available-update prompt to the front.
  • Launch at Login is enabled for new installs and remains an ordinary opt-out toggle in General Settings.

item.title: Version 1.9
item.description:
• Added thirds, two-thirds, Almost Maximize, configurable Center sizing, and repeated-press size cycling.
  • Move windows to the next or previous display and restore their pre-snap size from the menu or a shortcut.
  • Workspaces can be renamed and report restore results; app-rule positions can be edited in place.
  • Improved Electron and cross-display snapping with verified final frames, safer Accessibility handling, and clearer failure feedback.
  • Added clipboard number/delete controls and made File Shelf limits, disabled state, and stale-file cleanup consistent.
  • Redock 1.8 preferences migrate automatically to stable action IDs. This upgrade is one-way, so downgrading after opening 1.9 is not supported.

item.title: Version 1.8
item.description:
• The installer window now shows what to do, including the step everyone missed: open Redock from Applications, not from the disk image.
  • Redock refuses to run from the disk image instead of starting up and quietly failing later. Permissions granted there are discarded by macOS, which is why window snapping appeared broken for some people.
  • If you already dragged Redock to Applications, it offers to open that copy for you.

item.title: Version 1.7
item.description:
• Redock now updates itself, so you no longer have to download and reinstall by hand.
  • Fixed dragging a window to the screen edge doing nothing after granting permission. The permission was fine; macOS decides whether an app may watch for drags when it starts, so it needed a restart and nothing said so.
  • Redock now warns you if it is running from the disk image instead of your Applications folder, which quietly broke permissions.
  • Drag snapping keeps working with apps that are slow to respond or use a non-standard title bar.
